title: Serum Metabolites and Whole Blood Transcriptome in Metabolically Healthy Obesity (preprint)
coords: x and y are percent of the page image, measured from the top left
intro: Research Square preprint, 14 October 2024. Not peer-reviewed.

hotspots.title: What this is
hotspots.note: The authors compare serum metabolites and blood gene activity between an obesity group and lean controls. Research Square posted this preprint on 14 October 2024; it has not undergone peer review.

hotspots.title: The abstract
hotspots.note: The study enrolled 40 adults; 36 remained in the metabolite analysis after exclusions. The authors report 116 of 711 metabolites at p < 0.05 without multiple-testing correction, and differences in 14 of 26 blood gene-activity pathways.

hotspots.title: From 1,069 to 711 metabolites
hotspots.note: The lab profiled 1,069 metabolites. Excluding 174 unidentified metabolites and those with more than 20% missing data left 711.

hotspots.title: Outliers removed
hotspots.note: A principal component analysis flagged four samples as outliers: one lean control and three from the obesity group. That leaves 36 people for the metabolite analysis, 19 lean and 17 with obesity, not the 40 in the abstract.

hotspots.title: The gene-activity side
hotspots.note: Whole blood RNA was read on a microarray covering 32,304 genes. This part of the analysis uses 21 profiles, 11 lean and 10 with obesity, so it rests on fewer people than the metabolite part.

hotspots.title: Baseline: who was in the study
hotspots.note: Mean ages were 35.40 and 35.95 years, and mean BMIs were 23.31 and 40.43. The authors report a higher proportion of women in the obesity group (p ≤ 0.012).

hotspots.title: Table 1
hotspots.note: The enrolled groups differed in sex distribution: 14 men and 6 women in the lean group, 5 men and 15 women in the obesity group. The analysis adjusted for sex, age and BMI.

hotspots.title: 116 metabolites, no correction
hotspots.note: The authors report 116 of 711 metabolites at p < 0.05; 91 were higher in the obesity group. They did not correct for multiple testing, so these findings are exploratory.

hotspots.title: Table 2: pathways
hotspots.note: The authors group metabolites by biochemical pathway. Arginine, glutamate, and cysteine and methionine pathways have some of the smallest FDR p-values in this table.

hotspots.title: The authors' limits
hotspots.note: Small sample because of strict age matching, a single time point that cannot show cause, and blood only, which says little about specific tissues. The authors say the study needs repeating in larger, more varied groups.

hotspots.title: Who did what
hotspots.note: The preprint credits me and five co-authors with collecting, purifying and harmonizing samples. Other authors handled the computational analysis and writing.

hotspots.title: Figure 1: volcano plot and counts
hotspots.note: Each dot is a metabolite; higher means a smaller p-value. The bars count metabolites meeting the uncorrected p < 0.05 threshold. Lipids include 36 higher and 14 lower in the obesity group.

hotspots.title: Figure 2: sphingomyelins
hotspots.note: The figure shows higher levels of 15 sphingomyelins in the obesity group. Each pair of boxes represents one lipid; the comparisons are exploratory.

hotspots.title: Figure 4: pathway activity
hotspots.note: The bars show pathway scores derived from blood gene activity, with obesity in red and lean controls in teal.
